target_channel.name: Factify Shorts

niche: Curiosity, Science Mysteries, Extreme Phenomena, Weird Technology & Engineering Marvels

golden_rules_for_topics.description: Flexible rule system: not all videos need to satisfy all 3 rules. Rules apply dynamically based on video category.

curiosity_mystery.description: Space, biology quirks, weird science, what-if hypotheses
curiosity_mystery.visual_requirement: Smooth ambient/space/macro footage (does not require violent action)

odd_tech_engineering.description: Crazy machines, walking buildings, satisfying tools, construction secrets
odd_tech_engineering.hook_requirement: Fascinating/satisfying hook (does not need extreme life-or-death shock)

rule_1_curiosity_gap.name: The 3-Second Psychological Curiosity Gap
rule_1_curiosity_gap.requirement: Creates an immediate open loop or shock statement. Applied strictly to Extreme Viral shorts; applied as intriguing curiosity to Science/Tech shorts.

rule_2_visual_motion_appeal.name: High-Motion Real Footage Feasibility
rule_2_visual_motion_appeal.requirement: Requires dynamic video footage. For extreme topics: violent motion/action. For space/science: smooth cinematic macro/space visuals.

rule_3_universal_global_appeal.name: Universal Curiosity (Tier-1 USA & Global)
rule_3_universal_global_appeal.requirement: Subject matter must be globally fascinating and avoid hyper-local trivia.

topics.title: One Snap Can Cut a Ship in Half: The Mooring Snapback Danger
topics.hook: This ordinary looking ship rope is actually one of the deadliest weapons on water.
topics.core_fact: When a ship's high-tension mooring line snaps, it whips back at over 700 km/h with enough kinetic force to cut clean through human bone and steel railings.

topics.title: The Man Who Injected Snake Venom 200 Times
topics.hook: This man willingly let the world's deadliest snakes bite him over 200 times.
topics.core_fact: Tim Friede gradually immunized his body against lethal black mamba and cobra venom. His antibodies are now being used by scientists to formulate a universal antivenom.

topics.title: Why Buildings in China Literally Walk Across Streets
topics.hook: Engineers in China did not demolish this 7,600-ton historical building... they made it walk.
topics.core_fact: Using 198 robotic walking legs powered by computer hydraulics, the 85-year-old primary school moved 62 meters in 18 days to clear space for a modern development.

topics.title: What 500,000 Volts Looks Like Up Close
topics.hook: Never touch a powerline, unless you're wearing a suit made entirely of stainless steel mesh.
topics.core_fact: Linemen work on live 500kV power lines from helicopters wearing Faraday cage suits. Electricity flows around their body without shocking their internal organs.

topics.title: The Secret Chemical Injected Into Sinking Roads
topics.hook: Why are workers injecting this strange white foam under highway concrete?
topics.core_fact: It is high-density polyurethane foam. When injected into tiny drill holes, it expands with thousands of pounds of pressure, leveling sunk concrete slabs in under 15 minutes.

topics.title: What If Earth Stopped Spinning for Just 5 Seconds?
topics.hook: If the Earth stopped spinning for just five seconds, almost nothing on the surface would survive.
topics.core_fact: At the equator, everything is moving at 1,670 km/h. If Earth suddenly stopped, the atmosphere, oceans, and buildings would keep moving eastward at supersonic speed.

topics.title: The AI Robot That Kills 200,000 Weeds Per Hour With Lasers
topics.hook: Farmers are no longer spraying chemicals on crops. Instead, they unleash laser-firing killer robots.
topics.core_fact: Equipped with 12 high-powered CO2 lasers and computer vision, this autonomous tractor identifies and vaporizes 200,000 weeds per hour without damaging a single crop.

topics.title: The Floating Stone Island You Can't Find on Any Map
topics.hook: Sailors in the South Pacific suddenly sailed into what looked like solid land floating on water.
topics.core_fact: Underwater volcanic eruptions spew millions of tons of frothy pumice stone. Trapped gas bubbles make stone lighter than water, creating floating stone islands as big as Manhattan.

topics.title: Why Bats Can Never Stand Up or Walk
topics.hook: Have you ever wondered why you have never seen a bat walk like a bird?
topics.core_fact: Bat leg bones are so light and underdeveloped to facilitate flight that they cannot support their body weight. Their claws lock into place mechanically when hanging upside down, requiring zero muscle energy.

topics.title: Inside the Most Dangerous Job in the World: Saturation Diving
topics.hook: These workers live in a metal can for 30 days and breathe helium just to weld underwater pipes.
topics.core_fact: Saturation divers live in pressurized chambers at hundreds of meters depth. If they depressurize too fast, nitrogen bubbles in their blood would boil instantly.
